intent: Hold the iteration 4 geometry unchanged for the final race. It is the best-scoring design (67.90), it clears oval line losses, and the Integrator has said the geometry is at its limit, so the remaining gains must come from the controller. Keeping the geometry fixed also lets the Integrator's controller work transfer directly to the unseen track without any rebuild.
learning: Widening the sensor span from ±0.036 m to ±0.054 m removed oval line losses and improved oval progress, so sensing reach was a real constraint there. On s-bend and slalom the single line loss per run persisted at max_error about 0.065 to 0.067 m, which suggests turn authority and reach are both near their limits for those tracks. Future work should focus on the controller's response to the line loss and the speed, not on further geometry changes.
rationale: Iteration 4 is the best result so far (67.90, up from 55.14). Widening the five sensors to ±0.054 m at 0.027 m steps removed oval line losses (0.6 to 0.0) and lifted oval progress from 0.121 to 0.204, with oval max_error at 0.0625 m and no line loss. The s-bend and slalom still lost the line once per run (line_loss_events 1.0), with max_error 0.0669 and 0.0648 m. That is at or above the 0.06 m threshold the Integrator set, so the Integrator's rule now applies: the sensor reach is at its limit for those tracks. Earlier levers were already tried and did not clear them: mass 0.6 kg (iteration 2), wheel_track 0.09 m (iteration 3), and the wider span (iteration 4). The Integrator's latest feedback asks me to keep the ±0.054 m span with 0.027 m steps, mass 0.6 kg and wheel_track 0.09 m, and to leave the remaining gains to the controller. Iteration 5 is the final iteration and its design is what races on the unseen track, so an untested geometry change now carries risk and would force the Integrator to rebuild. I therefore keep the iteration 4 geometry exactly. Expected result: the same behaviour as iteration 4, which scored 67.9, with any gain coming from the Integrator's controller on the s-bend and slalom losses and the oval progress shortfall. The unseen track is different in shape, so the main uncertainty is whether the ±0.054 m reach holds on bends that are sharper than the development set.
